subject: Log shipping retention & Splunk HEC gateway onboarding
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Log shipping retention & Splunk HEC gateway onboarding

Alex —

Thanks for taking the time to kick this off. Per our call today, I wanted to capture the proposed approach for shipping logs and metrics from your private deployment (VPC) into Splunk while meeting Acme's retention/compliance constraints. High level: we recommend using a short-lived Splunk HEC gateway inside your VPC, TLS to Splunk HEC, and a snapshot/rollover policy for raw tokenized logs.

Quick summary of asks from your side:
- Allow outbound to Splunk HEC endpoints (TLS 443) from the forwarder subnet (we'll provide CIDR/ports).
- Confirm retention window targets (current ask: 365 days hot, 3 years cold archive).
- Who will manage HEC token rotation? (Acme or Redwood-managed with KMS-backed secrets).

Attached are two artifacts to review: redwood-splunk-hec-guide.pdf (architecture + sample firewall rules) and redwood-log-config-examples.yaml (our suggested rsyslog/Vector config and sample indexing keys).

Next steps proposed:
1) You confirm firewall/Egress policy and token rotation owner by EOD Thu.
2) We run a 2-hour onboarding session next Tue to validate ingest and index mappings.
3) If all good, we'll hand over a retention & snapshot runbook for your SREs.

If this matches your expectations I can loop in procurement for the SLA addendum.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Log shipping retention & Splunk HEC gateway onboarding

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from Acme:

- Retention: the business requires 2 years hot + 3 years cold (so 2y searchable, 3y archived). Is that compatible with your snapshot plan?
- Token rotation: our preference is to own the HEC tokens and rotate quarterly. We can use our KMS (AWS KMS) to store the token if Redwood supports retrieving it during agent startup.
- Firewall rules: please send exact CIDRs. We have strict egress auditing and will need a list for change control.

Also: can Redwood support digest/truncated payloads for PII-sensitive fields so we only store hashed values in Splunk's hot bucket? If so, please indicate where in the pipeline that masking happens.

We are fine to schedule the 2-hour onboarding next Tue; procurement will review the SLA addendum (cc'd).

Regards,
Alex Rivera
Director, Observability & Insights
Acme Retail

Alex / Naomi —

Quick technical notes from the infra side that should answer the two main items: token management and PII masking.

1) Token rotation & secret retrieval- We can integrate with Acme's AWS KMS. Our agent supports fetching a transient HEC token at startup via an IAM role that has decrypt permission on the KMS key. Operational modes:
  - Customer-managed tokens (preferred for Acme): Redwood agent fetches token on start, stores in-memory, rotates on signal.
  - Redwood-managed (alternate): Greenwood service issues tokens periodically and pushes via private API (requires approve on your side).

2) PII masking- Redwood provides an in-line masking hook in the log pipeline. Implementation options:
  - Mask at source: rsyslog/Vector filter (preferred for minimal data exposure).
  - Mask in-flight at the agent: regex/hash plugin before HEC payload is emitted.
  - Post-ingest transform: Splunk props/transforms (not recommended for compliance).

3) Firewall/CIDR- For the onboarding test, allow outbound to the following: 54.210.112.0/24, 54.210.113.0/24 (HEC gateway ELBs in us-west-2) ports 443. We'll provide a signed IP list for prod.

4) Retention model- We'll implement a two-tier snapshot: daily hot snapshots (searchable) with 2y retention, and weekly cold exports to S3 Glacier with a 3y retention policy. The runbook includes an automated restore/test cadence.

Marissa is copied for runbook delivery and automated test creation.

Vivek
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
